newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS: U.S. oil firms set restarts after hurricane.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS: U.S. oil firms set restarts after hurricane.

text.p: Oil producers on the U.S. Gulf began scheduling restarts at platforms and other facilities after shutting down operations ahead of Hurricane Danny's arrival.

The Louisiana Offshort Oil Port (LOOP) expects to have offshore operations back to normal on Saturday. One ship was scheduled was to offload crude Friday, though that has been delayed until the facility is returned to operation.

Texaco Inc said it was returning 365 workers to 10 rigs in the Gulf after evacuating them Thursday, and operations were seen returing to normal during the weekend. About 40,000 barrels of oil and 200 million cubic feet of natural gas per day were affected, the company said.

Mobil Corp expected production would be back up by the weekend at six offshore fields shut Thursday. Those fields included Eugene Island 240, Green Canyon 18/60, Ship Shoal 72, Ship Shoal 182 and Main Pass fields 6/103 and 73.

Exxon Corp said it had suffered modest production losses at its onshore Grand Isle, Louisiana facilities, and that its 432,000 barrel per day Baton Rouge refinery had taken precautionary measures but operations there were unaffected.

Chevron Corp said it would have its 295,000 barrel per day refinery in Pascagoula, Mississippi shut by 2300 GMT Friday as precautionary measure, although the company would not estimate a restart time for the facility or comment on the length of time a full restart would take.

The hurricane was inching its way northeast toward Mobile Bay, Alabama at about 5 miles (8 km) per hour, with sustained winds of 75 mph (120 kmph). Hurricane watches remain in effect from Morgan City, Louisiana to Destin, Florida. The storm is expected to weaken as it moves over land sometime Saturday.
